hints.content:
The basic function $\sin(x)$ intersects its midline at $(0,0)$ and has a maximum point at $\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2},1\right)$.

$\qquad$![](${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/06941548a579199b78346bf8e7ed0476.png)

Let's transform $\pink{\sin(x)}$ to $\blue{3\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{5} x+\dfrac{2\pi}{5}\right)-3}$ step by step and see how the graph changes along the way.

The transformation from $\pink{\sin(x)}$ to $\green{\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{5} x\right)}$ is a horizontal stretch by a factor of $\dfrac{5}{\pi}$, so the maximum point's horizontal distance from the origin is stretched from $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ to $\dfrac{\pi}{2}\cdot\dfrac{5}{\pi}=2.5$.

$\qquad$[[☃ image 1]]

The transformation from $\green{\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{5} x\right)}$ to $\red{3\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{5} x\right)}$ is a vertical stretch by a factor of $3$, so the maximum point's vertical distance from the origin is stretched from $1$ to $3$.

$\qquad$[[☃ image 2]]

options.alt: A dashed graph and a solid graph trigonometric wave on an x y coordinate plane. The x axis scales by one and the y axis scales by one. On the dashed graph there is a point on the graph at the midline at (zero, zero) and a point on the maximum next to the mentioned point at (pi over two, one). On the solid graph, there is a point on the graph at the midline at (zero, zero) and a point at the maximum next to the mentioned point at (two and one half, one).

A dashed graph and a solid graph trigonometric wave on an x y coordinate plane. The x axis scales by one and the y axis scales by one. On the dashed graph there is a point on the graph at the midline at (zero, zero) and a point at the maximum next to the mentioned point at (two and one half, one). On the solid graph, there is a point on the graph at the midline at (zero, zero) and a point at the maximum next to the mentioned point at (two and one half, three).

hints.content: The transformation from $\red{3\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{5} x\right)}$ to $\blue{3\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{5} x+\dfrac{2\pi}{5}\right)-3}$, which is equivalent to $3\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{5} (x+2)\right)-3$, is a translation to the left by $2$ units and a translation downwards by $3$ units.

As a result of these transformations, the intersection point with the midline is now at $\left(-2,-3\right)$ and the maximum point is at $(0.5,0)$.

The resulting graph looks as follows:

$\qquad$[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A graph of a trigonometric wave on an x y coordinate plane. The x axis scales by one and the y axis scales by one. There is a point on the graph at the midline at (negative two, negative three) and a point on the maximum next to the mentioned point at (one half, zero).

question.content:
**Graph $g(x)=3\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{5} x+\dfrac{2\pi}{5}\right)-3$ in the interactive widget.**  
*Note that one moveable point always defines an extremum point in the graph and the other point always defines a neighbouring intersection with the midline.*
